findings.title: Critical snapshot schema rejects valid zero nonbranch group dimensions
findings.contract: Authority followup: critical coverage is branch-only >=95; safe zero nonbranch dimensions remain valid.
findings.observation: For each of statements, lines and functions, set total=covered=0 on every member of the approved kernel group; all global dimensions remain positive and branches remain 100%. The native producer returns PASS. snapshotSchema rejects with hiso:snapshot_types:coverage-critical. The unchanged public critical-coverage CLI returns exit 0/PASS for zero functions, then native snapshot admission rejects its output.
findings.cause: The group uses the same metrics schema as global coverage; it requires a positive denominator and numeric pct in every dimension. Native critical aggregation correctly emits pct:null for valid nonbranch zero.
findings.impact: A valid native critical report cannot cross producer/verifier admission. This directly violates the authorized acceptance bar.
findings.recommendation: Separate critical group metric validation from positive global metric validation; allow only safe nonbranch zero with covered=0 and pct=null, while retaining branch denominators, raw95 and invalid-counter rejection.

findings.title: Malformed optional skipped counters are accepted by critical producer and snapshot admission
findings.contract: All invalid counters still fail; malformed members must poison aggregates.
findings.observation: A selected critical member with branches.skipped=-1, 0.5, 9007199254740992 or string "0" produces PASS and passes snapshotSchema. An unchanged public critical CLI emits exit 0/PASS for skipped=-1 and native snapshot admission accepts that receipt.
findings.cause: validCounters validates total/covered only; critical file schemas do not validate skipped. Producer reconstruction preserves but does not reject the malformed field.
findings.impact: Critical gate receipts can contain invalid counters. aggregateCoverage independently rejects these skipped values if they appear in its canonical coverage inputs, so this observation does not establish a complete remote-CI bypass.
findings.recommendation: Validate skipped when present using the native safe nonnegative integer and policy constraints; preserve compatibility with native reports that omit this optional field.

findings.title: Legacy importer marks PostgreSQL and chaos reports PASS before checking their pass-only policy
findings.contract: The native producer/importer/verifier contract must retain PostgreSQL and chaos pass-only semantics.
findings.observation: Fresh coherent legacy content seals are verified with verifyGateSeals before each native importer CLI. A postgres pending case and a chaos todo case each produce exit 0 and manifest.status=PASS with copied outputs and entry.skipped=0. Native verifySnapshots then rejects each with hiso:required_skip. The unit missing-occurrence control returns FAIL and emits no unit/legacy PASS outputs; governed unit pending is preserved correctly.
findings.cause: The importer applies shared case admission to unit only. Other sealed test reports are copied and marked PASS without gateTestReport admission.
findings.impact: Importer PASS and its skip counts are false for these required reports. The final native verifier still rejects the selected snapshots; no full CI acceptance is claimed.
findings.recommendation: Apply frozen-selector exact membership and pass-only report validation to postgres/chaos before copying outputs or emitting an imported PASS manifest.

findings.title: Mutation snapshot admission does not bind receipt hashes or selected risk inventory
findings.contract: Proper mutation sourceHash binding and no reduced denominators/risk-domain inventory.
findings.observation: The native current mutation manifest validates all ten entries and their source hashes; replacing any current manifest sourceSha256 with zeros is rejected. In contrast, a native-shaped PASS receipt with current run/candidate fields is accepted by snapshotSchema and verifySnapshots after changing mutations[0].sourceSha256 to zeros, changing manifestSha256 to zeros, or reducing the receipt to one killed coverage mutation and domains=["coverage"]. These are inert JSON receipts; no mutation driver or mutated code is executed.
findings.cause: The snapshot schema checks counts agree and rows are KILLED but does not compare the receipt against the authoritative manifest, source hashes, IDs or required domains. verifySnapshots only requires its PASS verdict.
findings.impact: Snapshot admission cannot distinguish a stale/unbound or reduced mutation receipt from the current full mutation inventory. This is demonstrated at native admission, not by obtaining remote trust, signatures or an overall CI PASS.
findings.recommendation: Bind receipt manifestSha256, exact mutation IDs/domains and per-entry source/hash/selector metadata to the frozen authoritative manifest, retaining its current sourceHash validation.

findings.title: IEEE-754 division admits a safe-integer branch ratio mathematically below 95
findings.contract: Critical branch threshold is an inclusive raw 95%, with safe integer counters.
findings.observation: A complete 281-path synthetic coverage summary has approval-group total=9007199254700003 and covered=8556839291965002. All file and global sums are safe. Exact integer evidence gives 100*covered=855683929196500200 < 95*total=855683929196500285. Native floating division nevertheless yields 95; producer, unchanged public critical CLI and snapshot admission accept PASS.
findings.cause: The producer and independent verifier both evaluate the floating quotient times 100, which loses the below-boundary distinction at large safe integers.
findings.impact: The raw inclusive threshold is not exact across its explicitly accepted safe-integer range. Normal-sized supplied 94.999/95/95.001 controls behave correctly; this is a numerical edge, not evidence of ordinary measured coverage below the floor.
findings.recommendation: For the normative integer 95 threshold, compare exact integer products without Number overflow (for example using BigInt) in both producer and verifier; retain display percentages separately.

positiveObservations: 414 supplied cases pass unmodified, with zero pending/todo.
Exact unit membership includes files, names and duplicate-title occurrence IDs; missing occurrence is rejected before importer unit output emission.
Governed unit pending/skipped/todo parity works in producer, importer and verifier; none-policy remains strict.
Shared native producer/report validators and final snapshot verifier reject required PostgreSQL/chaos skips.
Fractional/unsafe/negative total and covered members and unsafe aggregates are rejected; valid neighbors do not rescue poisoned total/covered dimensions.
Ordinary 94.999% branch coverage is rejected while 95% and 95.001% are accepted.
All ten current mutation manifest source hashes and unique selectors match; current manifest drift is refused.
Source, dependencies, dist and all recorded mtimes/modes/sizes are unchanged before/after.
limitations: No network, real PostgreSQL, provider, real data, secrets, push, deployment or production validation.
No complete four-scope remote trusted aggregate executed; semantic observations do not assert an overall CI bypass.
Main 8400 comparison is attributed to the Lead; independent measurements and hashes are of Packet Source only.
Mutation driver execution is intentionally excluded; source/manifest bindings and inert receipt admission are tested.
